Single-objective optimization

Find an approximate second-order stationary point of the full objective:

\textbf{Status.} Polynomial gap present; Bounds missing; Joint budget unresolved

\textbf{Gap classes present.} Polynomial gap; Logarithmic gap

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}
\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}
Find an approximate second-order stationary point of the full objective:


\AtlasMath{\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2\le\varepsilon_g,\qquad\nabla^2f(\widehat{x})\succeq-\varepsilon_H I_d.}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}
The population objective \AtlasInlineMath{f(x)=\mathbb{E}_Z[\ell(x;Z)]} is bounded below.

The objective has a finite infimum, and the public initial point \AtlasInlineMath{x_0} satisfies \AtlasInlineMath{f(x_0)-\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)\le\Delta}.

On a common probability-one event, all sample gradients are \AtlasInlineMath{\beta}-Lipschitz and all sample Hessians are \AtlasInlineMath{M_2}-Lipschitz at every point. Differentiation and expectation may be interchanged.

Sample errors satisfy \AtlasInlineMath{\|\nabla\ell(x;Z)-\nabla f(x)\|_2\le\sigma_1} and \AtlasInlineMath{\|\nabla^2\ell(x;Z)-\nabla^2f(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\sigma_2}, with \AtlasInlineMath{\sup_x\|\nabla f(x)\|_2\le G}.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}
An opaque persistent handle \AtlasInlineMath{a} can be requested for free without revealing sample data. Distinct new handles bind independent samples \AtlasInlineMath{Z_a}. At each call, choose an existing handle and any point \AtlasInlineMath{(a,x)}, then request the full \AtlasInlineMath{\nabla\ell(x;Z_a)} or full \AtlasInlineMath{\nabla^2\ell(x;Z_a)}, charged separately. A handle may be reused at arbitrarily many points.

No sample value, internal sample data or third derivative is returned. An observed full matrix may be used freely in internal linear algebra.

The public inputs are \AtlasInlineMath{x_0}, the target accuracy, and \AtlasInlineMath{d}, \AtlasInlineMath{\Delta}, \AtlasInlineMath{\beta}, \AtlasInlineMath{M_2}, \AtlasInlineMath{\sigma_1}, \AtlasInlineMath{\sigma_2}, \AtlasInlineMath{G}, \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_g}, \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_H}. Numerical constants are admissible bounds and need not equal the sharp constants of the instance. The objective, unqueried derivatives, minimizer and minimum value are hidden.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}
Return \AtlasInlineMath{\widehat{x}\in \mathbb{R}^d}.

The output may be an unqueried point, a feasible average of past iterates, or another feasible postprocessing result. No function value or additional computable certificate is required.

The algorithm may output the failure symbol \AtlasInlineMath{\bot}; this event counts toward the failure probability.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}
The base error is


\AtlasMath{\mathcal{E}(\widehat{x})=\max\left\{\frac{\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2}{\varepsilon_g},\frac{[-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(\widehat{x}))]_+}{\varepsilon_H}\right\}.}


\AtlasInlineMath{[a]_+=\max\{a,0\}}, and \AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_{\min}} denotes the smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix. The target is \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{E}(\widehat{x})\le1}, where \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_g} and \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_H} are independent positive tolerances.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}
The native cost is the joint resource vector \AtlasInlineMath{(N_g,N_H)}, counting full sample gradients and full sample Hessians separately. Requesting both derivatives at one point costs two calls, as does evaluating the same handle at two points for a difference.

The total-cost projection is explicitly \AtlasInlineMath{N_g+N_H}. Separate budgets for \AtlasInlineMath{N_g} and \AtlasInlineMath{N_H} may also be displayed, but displaying one coordinate does not make the other operation free. All coordinatewise upper bounds must be attained by the same algorithm.

The resource budget is a fixed worst-case cap on every execution path. Initialization, stopping checks, and all actual responses in a batch are included.

Arithmetic, linear algebra, tensor operations, storage, and global solution of known models are free. Bit complexity, communication, and wall-clock time are not counted.

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}
Arbitrary measurable adaptive algorithms with private randomness are allowed.

No linear-span, Krylov or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Memory and internal computation are unrestricted.

Information is acquired adaptively in query order. Parallel submission does not reduce the number of actual responses counted. There is no communication-round or memory budget. Exact real arithmetic and arbitrarily small positive query separations are allowed.

Choose one algorithm from the public inputs, then require its guarantee separately for every admissible instance and oracle law.


\AtlasMath{\Pr\!\left[\max\left\{\frac{\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2}{\varepsilon_g},\frac{[-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(\widehat{x}))]_+}{\varepsilon_H}\right\}\le 1\right]\ge\frac23.}


Expectation or probability is evaluated after fixing the instance; randomness comes from the algorithm's private seed and oracle sampling.

The running-cost guarantee is specified separately under RESOURCE.

\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}
\AtlasInlineMath{x,\widehat{x},x_0}: Query or decision point, algorithm output, and public initial point. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{R}^d}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{R}^d}: Real coordinate space; vectors use the Euclidean norm unless otherwise stated. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d} is a positive integer.

\AtlasInlineMath{\langle u,v\rangle,\ \|u\|_2}: Euclidean inner product and norm.


\AtlasMath{\langle u,v\rangle=u^\top v,\qquad\|u\|_2=\sqrt{\langle u,u\rangle}.}


\AtlasInlineMath{D^jf(x),\ \nabla f(x),\ \nabla^2f(x)}: Fréchet derivative of order \AtlasInlineMath{j}, gradient and Hessian. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{j\in\{0,\ldots,2\}} and \AtlasInlineMath{D^0f=f}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}},\ \|T\|_{\mathrm{op},2}}: Induced operator norm of a Euclidean multilinear tensor; the spectral norm for matrices.


\AtlasMath{\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{op},2}=\sup_{\|u_1\|_2,\ldots,\|u_j\|_2\le1}|T[u_1,\ldots,u_j]|.}


\AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal{E}}: Base error defined in the metric specification; expectation or probability aggregation is imposed by the guarantee.

\AtlasInlineMath{N}: Total number of original oracle calls; the unit cost is specified in the resource convention. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{T^*}: Minimum worst-case budget for one algorithm to meet the requirement on the full instance class, within the specified regime, guarantee and resource projection. Expected-resource specifications instead minimize the per-instance expected budget.

\AtlasInlineMath{O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde{O}}: Asymptotic upper bounds, lower bounds, matching bounds up to constants, and upper bounds omitting the declared logarithmic factors. \textbf{Domain:} Hidden constants, fixed parameters, and omitted logarithmic variables are specified for each bound.

\AtlasInlineMath{\inf,\sup,\min,\max}: Infimum, supremum, attained minimum and attained maximum.

\AtlasInlineMath{c,C}: Positive universal constants without assigned numerical values; a subscript permits dependence only on the indicated fixed parameters. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<c,C<\infty}.

\AtlasInlineMath{f,f^*}: Unknown objective and its global infimum over the specified feasible domain.


\AtlasMath{f^*=\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x).}


\AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb{E},\Pr}: Expectation and probability after fixing the instance; their randomness sources are specified by the guarantee.

\AtlasInlineMath{Z,\ell(x;Z)}: Sample random variable and the associated scalar sample loss.


\AtlasMath{f(x)=\mathbb{E}_Z\ell(x;Z).}


\AtlasInlineMath{a,Z_a}: Opaque persistent handle and its associated hidden sample.

\AtlasInlineMath{N_g,N_H}: Numbers of full sample-gradient and full sample-Hessian evaluations. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{N_g,N_H\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\bot}: Output symbol explicitly declaring algorithmic failure.

\AtlasInlineMath{u\preceq v}: Coordinatewise order for resource vectors; the same symbol for symmetric matrices denotes the positive semidefinite order.


\AtlasMath{u\preceq v\iff u_i\le v_i\quad\text{for every }i.}


\AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_{\min}(A),[z]_+}: The smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix and the positive part of a scalar.


\AtlasMath{[z]_+=\max\{z,0\}.}


\AtlasInlineMath{I_d}: The identity matrix in dimension \AtlasInlineMath{d}.

\AtlasInlineMath{d}: Ambient dimension; dimension requirements are stated separately for each bound. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{d\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge 1}}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\Delta}: Upper bound on the difference between the objective value at the known initial point and its global infimum. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\Delta>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\beta}: Common Lipschitz upper bound for the gradients of all sample losses. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\beta>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{M_2}: Common Lipschitz upper bound for the Hessians of all sample losses. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{M_2>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\sigma_1}: Almost-sure bound on the sample gradient's deviation from the population gradient. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\sigma_1>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\sigma_2}: Almost-sure operator-norm bound on the sample Hessian's deviation from the population Hessian. \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\sigma_2>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{G}: Global upper bound on the population gradient norm \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{G>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_g}: Gradient tolerance \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_g>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_H}: Curvature tolerance \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{\varepsilon_H>0}.

\AtlasInlineMath{\theta}: Fixed group of positive model bounds.


\AtlasMath{\theta=(\Delta,\beta,M_2,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,G).}


\AtlasInlineMath{B_g}: Dimensionless leading term in one algorithm's gradient-evaluation budget.


\AtlasMath{B_g=1+\frac{\Delta\beta+\sigma_1^2}{\varepsilon_g^2}+\frac{\sigma_1\beta\Delta}{\varepsilon_g^3}+\frac{\beta^2\Delta}{\varepsilon_g^2\varepsilon_H}.}


\AtlasInlineMath{B_H}: Dimensionless leading term in one algorithm's Hessian-evaluation budget.


\AtlasMath{B_H=1+\frac{\Delta\beta}{\varepsilon_g^2}+\frac{\sigma_2^2}{\varepsilon_H^2}+\frac{\sigma_2M_2\Delta}{\varepsilon_g\varepsilon_H^2}+\frac{2M_2^2\Delta}{\varepsilon_H^3}.}


\AtlasInlineMath{T,\Lambda}: Iteration cap and shared logarithmic factor.


\AtlasMath{T=\left\lceil1+48\Delta\left(\frac{32\beta}{3\varepsilon_g^2}+\frac{12M_2^2}{\varepsilon_H^3}\right)\right\rceil,\quad\Lambda=1+\log[C(d+1)(T+1)].}


\AtlasInlineMath{s_*}: Positive scale used in the lower-bound construction.


\AtlasMath{s_*=\min\{1,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,\beta,M_2,G\}.}


\AtlasInlineMath{D_g}: Logarithmic dimension factor in the persistent-handle gradient hard construction.


\AtlasMath{D_g=C\log(2+\Delta/\varepsilon_g+\Delta s_*^2/\varepsilon_g^3).}


\AtlasInlineMath{d_*}: Sufficient dimension threshold for the lower-bound construction; an existential constant function, not a supplied numerical value.


\AtlasMath{d_*\le C(\theta)\left[1+\frac{\Delta D_g^{3/4}}{\varepsilon_g}+\varepsilon_H^{-4}\log(2/\varepsilon_H)+\varepsilon_H^{-3}\right].}

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy Translate the public initial point to the origin. Set e=\allowbreak{}epsilon\_\allowbreak{}g,\allowbreak{} b=\allowbreak{}sigma\_\allowbreak{}1/\allowbreak{}2 and t=\allowbreak{}x\_\allowbreak{}1-(x\_\allowbreak{}0)\_\allowbreak{}1. For hypotheses h=\allowbreak{}+2e and h=\allowbreak{}-2e,\allowbreak{} let independent handle variables Z take values +/\allowbreak{}-b with mean h. Define ell\_\allowbreak{}h(x;\allowbreak{}Z)=\allowbreak{}4e*sqrt(1+t\textasciicircum{}2)+Z*t,\allowbreak{} independent of all other coordinates. Its population objective is 4e*sqrt(1+t\textasciicircum{}2)+h*t.\par\endgroup

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Native item 2}
Native pointer: /proofs/0/proof\_\allowbreak{}steps/1; canonical SHA-256: 575ac83107ad71ed2c1132086cfbf09a2c6daf7a8b993816824b20a0909fd8c1

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy These populations have finite minima 2*sqrt(3)*e and initial gap (4-2*sqrt(3))*e. Their gradient norm is at most 6e. Each sample Hessian has only entry 4e*(1+t\textasciicircum{}2)\textasciicircum{}(-3/\allowbreak{}2),\allowbreak{} so sample-gradient Lipschitz constant is at most 4e and sample-Hessian Lipschitz constant is at most 12e. Gradient noise is at most b+2e<=\allowbreak{}sigma\_\allowbreak{}1;\allowbreak{} Hessian noise is zero. Differentiation commutes with expectation. The r7 inequalities therefore ensure every fixed-contract assumption. Only the population must be bounded below;\allowbreak{} individual sample losses need not be.\par\endgroup

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Native item 3}
Native pointer: /proofs/0/proof\_\allowbreak{}steps/2; canonical SHA-256: 2f1a1238c84c5c744144e44afc11eff165dd4111741b0c8285d9f23656681702

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy The population Hessian is positive semidefinite,\allowbreak{} so any positive epsilon\_\allowbreak{}H is allowed. Under h=\allowbreak{}+2e,\allowbreak{} any successful output must have t<0;\allowbreak{} under h=\allowbreak{}-2e it must have t>0. Failure symbols count as failure. Thus success probability >=\allowbreak{}2/\allowbreak{}3 separately on both admissible instances yields a test with total variation at least 1/\allowbreak{}3.\par\endgroup

\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Native item 4}
Native pointer: /proofs/0/proof\_\allowbreak{}steps/3; canonical SHA-256: 7c7f6249b118f08550a2dec5a6976bbdb87e4aa99b265cd41cc9101a580a7008

\begingroup\raggedright\sloppy All Hessian responses are deterministic and identical under both hypotheses,\allowbreak{} even at arbitrary adaptive points. The first gradient query on a handle reveals its single Z;\allowbreak{} later gradient queries on that handle add no information.
